context: In 0-1 knapsack, each item can be taken at most once. This diagram uses a separate example from the previous figure and the main program: cap = 30, with three items weighing 10, 20, and 20 and worth 60, 110, and 120, respectively (see table). State dp[i, c] gives the maximum value using the first i items with available capacity c. The figure labels the columns wgt[i] and val[i] with item numbers starting at 1. The code accesses the arrays at index i-1.

When the current item fits, take the larger of dp[i-1, c] for skipping it and dp[i-1, c-wgt[i-1]] + val[i-1] for taking it. If it does not fit, only the skip branch is available. With no items (i = 0) or no capacity (c = 0), return 0.
description: Starting at root dp[3, 30], decide on item 3 (pineapple, weight 20, value 120), item 2 (watermelon, weight 20, value 110), then item 1 (apple, weight 10, value 60). Items 2 and 3 both weigh 20. Skipping item 3 and taking item 2 (dp[3, 30] → dp[2, 30] → dp[1, 10]) uses the same weight as taking item 3 and skipping item 2 (dp[3, 30] → dp[2, 10] → dp[1, 10]). Both use 20 units, leaving capacity 10 and only item 1 to consider. The paths meet at the same subproblem dp[1, 10].

Brute-force search does not save solved subproblems. Both occurrences of dp[1, 10] expand, each comparing dp[0, 10] for skipping item 1 with dp[0, 0] + 60 for taking it. The entire subproblem dp[1, 10] expands twice, duplicating the work.

At dp[2, 10] in the right subtree, item 2 weighs 20 but only 10 units of capacity remain. The node dp[1, -10] labeled “Prune: item weight > knapsack capacity” illustrates the excluded overweight branch. Before recursing, the code checks the weight and calls only the skip branch dp[1, 10], so it never makes a negative-capacity call.
The tables below list the input for this example and the full recursion tree as drawn. Row headers give the choices from the root to distinguish separate occurrences of a state.

frames.explanation: The figure has 13 nodes. Six are base-case leaves returning 0, and one illustrates the overweight branch. From the input, taking items 1 and 3 gives total weight 10 + 20 = 30 and maximum value 60 + 120 = 180. The tree nodes do not label the value 180 directly.
